3. This application has been filed by the Appellant Safi Mohd. @ Guddu Ansari S/o Salauddin,
under Section 389 Cr.P.C. read with Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeking suspension of sentence during pendency of the appeal in respect of case FIR No.188/2019 registered at P.S. Aman Vihar under Sections 363/366/376(2)(n) IPC and Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act,
2012 (POCSO Act), on multiple grounds.

sentences.text: On merits, learned counsel states that there are several contradictions and discrepancies in the testimony of the prosecutrix between the statements given under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and Section 164 Cr.P.C. as well as during the examination-in-chief and cross-examination before the Trial Court and reading of the statements and testimonies shows that the relationship between the prosecutrix and the Appellant was consensual.

There is no medical or scientific evidence on record to support the case of the prosecution and therefore, the conviction is illegal and the Appellant be released on bail as he is suffering incarceration for the last nearly 05 years.

Learned counsel also relies on a bail order granted by this Court on 04.05.2022 during the pendency of the trial, noting the contradictions in the testimony of the witnesses, however, as the Appellant was unable to furnish the bail bonds, he was never released.

6. Learned APP for the State, on the other hand, submits that the order granting regular bail cannot be relied upon at this stage since during trial, Appellant was under a presumption of innocence while today he is a convict and the threshold for seeking suspension of sentence is much higher.

It is further stated that the mere absence of forensic, medical and/or scientific evidence cannot be a ground to seek suspension as it is a settled law that sole testimony of the prosecutrix can be the basis of conviction.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 19/02/2024 at 23:52:45 7.
Heard.

8. Without adverting to the merits of the case, as the arguments raised by the Appellant on the alleged contradiction in the testimonies of the prosecution witnesses is a matter to be decided at the time of hearing the appeal, this Court is of the opinion that since the Appellant has undergone almost half of the sentence awarded and the appeal is likely to take time, it would be in the interest of justice, in view of the directions of the Supreme Court in Sonadhar (supra) and Saudan Singh (supra) to suspend the sentence of the Appellant.

In Bhagwan Rama Shinde Gosai v. State of Gujarat, (1999) 4 SCC 421, the Supreme Court has held that in cases where expeditious hearing of appeals cannot be effectuated, the Appellate Court should concern itself in considering suspension of sentence applications.
